LESSON: KENYAN INDIGENOUS GAMES (OPTIONAL)

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.1: Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional), part of Strand 11 in Grade 7 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: How does indigenous rope skipping enhance physical fitness? 2. Why is rope skipping considered an indigenous game?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify types of indigenous rope games played in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform different indigenous rope games for skill acquisition

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform indigenous rope skipping to a musical rhythm for enjoyment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role played by indigenous rope skipping games for fitness and health.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify types of indigenous rope games played in Kenya,

   Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. perform different indigenous rope games for skill acquisition

   Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. perform indigenous rope skipping to a musical rhythm for enjoyment,

   Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the role played by indigenous rope skipping games for fitness and health.

   Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous rope skipping and identify the skills observed,

2. demonstrate indigenous rope skipping skills while observing safety,

3. practise indigenous rope skipping while observing safety,

4. practise different types of indigenous rope skipping while combining it to a musical rhythm. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous rope skipping and identify the skills observed,
2. demonstrate indigenous rope skipping skills while observing safety,
3. practise indigenous rope skipping while observing safety,
4. practise different types of indigenous rope skipping while combining it to a musical rhythm. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Kenyan Indigenous Games (Optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Responsibility: the learner takes on different roles during indigenous rope skipping.

• Unity: the learner works with others in indigenous rope skipping.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: the learner observes safety rules of indigenous rope skipping.

• Health and Fitness: the learner improves fitness through indigenous rope skipping for a healthy lifestyle.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematics: the learner keeps counting during indigenous rope skipping.
